rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi connects these clauses to the preceding warning about careless prayer, framing showing off and withholding as its continuation.
rows.anchor: ثم وصل به قوله { فَوَيْلٌ لّلْمُصَلّينَ الذين هُمْ عَن صلاتهم سَاهُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns hypocrites who do not pray privately because they do not believe prayer obligatory, but pray publicly to be seen.
rows.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها ، ويصلونها علانية رياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says these hypocrites only outwardly join the praying, neglect prayer without seeking nearness to God or fulfilling its duty, mechanically bow and rise, display compliance, and withhold zakat and useful goods.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة وهم غافلون عن صلاتهم

rows.speaker: أنس والحسن
rows.claim: Anas and al-Hasan praise عن صلاتهم rather than في صلاتهم: عن means neglect amounting to abandonment and inattention, a hypocrite trait; في would mean lapses during prayer from satanic whispering or self-talk, which no Muslim escapes.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس والحسن قالا : الحمد لله الذي قال { عَن صلاتهم } ولم يقل «في صلاتهم »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi adds that the Prophet himself experienced forgetfulness in prayer, let alone others.
rows.anchor: وذلك لا يخلو عنه مسلم . وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقع له السهو في صلاته فضلاً عن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riyā is a reciprocal form of irāʾa: the show-off displays his deed to people, who respond by showing praise and admiration.
rows.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله ، وهم يرونه الثناء عليه والإعجاب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public performance of obligatory prayers is not showing off since they should be announced; voluntary worship is better concealed, unless displayed to encourage imitation.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض ، فمن حقها الإعلان بها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Nasafi cites the Prophet’s wording ولا غمة في فرائض الله to support openly announcing divine obligations; he states no grading.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  ولا غمة في فرائض الله  "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi glosses al-maʿūn as zakat.
rows.anchor: والماعون : الزكاة . وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets al-maʿūn as commonly borrowed household implements such as an axe, pot, bucket, and fire striker.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : ما يتعاور في العادة من الفأس والقدر والدلو والمقدحة ونحوها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha interprets al-maʿūn as water, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها : الماء والنار والملح والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi identifies Sūrat Abī Lahab as Meccan and says it has five verses.
rows.anchor: سورة أبي لهب مكية ، وهي خمس آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabba means ruin; an Arabic expression he cites describes someone ruined by old age, and he glosses the hands as perished.
rows.anchor: التباب : الهلاك ، ومنه قولهم : أشابّة أم تابّة ، أي هالكة من الهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Abu Lahab picked up a stone to throw at the Prophet, explaining the ruin of his hands.
rows.anchor: لأنه فيما يروى أخذ حجراً ليرمي به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi also glosses وَتَبَّ as meaning that Abu Lahab himself perished completely.
rows.anchor: { وَتَبَّ } وهلك كله ، أو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the hands are made ruined while the intended meaning is the ruin of his whole person, as in the expression cited from 22:10.
rows.anchor: أو جعلت يداه هالكتين ، والمراد هلاك جملته ، كقوله { بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi glosses وَتَبَّ as “that happened and came to pass”; the quoted poetic line uses وقد فعل to illustrate this sense.
rows.anchor: جزاء الكلاب العاويات وقد فعل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading وَقَد تَبَّ supports the sense that the ruin had indeed come to pass.
rows.anchor: وقد دلت عليه قراءة ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : { وَقَد تَبَّ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 26:214 was revealed, Muhammad summoned Quraysh at Ṣafā, elicited their trust in his warning, warned them of the Hour, and Abu Lahab rebuked him; this sūra was then revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل :{ وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } رقى الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya is an honorific, used because Abu Lahab was better known by it than by his personal name.
rows.anchor: وإنما كناه والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بها دون الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he was given a kunya to avoid his disliked personal name, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.
rows.anchor: أو لكراهة اسمه ، فاسمه عبد العزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that his fate in a fire of flames made the kunya fit his condition.
rows.anchor: أو لأن مآله إلى نار ذات لهب فوافقت حاله كنيته

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Nasafi attributes the form أبي لهب to the Meccan reader (Makkī).
rows.anchor: فوافقت حاله كنيته . { أَبِي لَهَبٍ } مكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ما is negative, saying Abu Lahab’s wealth did not avail him.
rows.anchor: للنفي { وَمَا كَسَبَ } مرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi says وَمَا كَسَبَ is nominative; ما may be relative, meaning what he acquired, or a verbal noun, meaning his acquisition.
rows.anchor: موصولة أو مصدرية ، أي ومكسوبه أو وكسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth that failed him may be what he inherited from his father, what he earned himself, or his old and newly acquired wealth.
rows.anchor: أي لم ينفعه ماله الذي ورثه من أبيه ، أو الذي كسبه بنفسه ، أو ماله التالد والطارف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that what Abu Lahab acquired means his children.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما كسب ولده

rows.speaker: أبو لهب
rows.claim: An unattributed report quotes Abu Lahab saying that if his nephew’s claim were true, he would ransom himself from it with his wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقاً فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي
